summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for acute volume overload with 14 pounds of weight gain and lower extremity edema, along with a painful right leg hematoma after trauma. She was treated with IV furosemide, achieving a net negative fluid balance of 2.1 liters. Her kidney function temporarily worsened, with creatinine rising to 1.9, but improved to 1.8 by discharge. Heart function remained stable with LVEF of 51%, and transplant ultrasound was normal. Pain from the leg contusion was managed with hydromorphone, and she was discharged home with instructions to hold diuretics for two days, restart at a lower dose, and follow up for lab monitoring. Immunosuppressant levels were therapeutic, and all chronic medications were continued.
problems: Contusion of right lower leg, initial encounter
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
